The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=1$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=0$ and $x=2.$*

${f}^{′}(1)≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x+h)-f(x-h)}{2h},
$$

at the point $x=1$ with step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(1) & ≈\frac{f(1+1)-f(1-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{f(2)-f(0)}{2} \\  & =\frac{3-(-1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{4}{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
